entities.summary:
The Spanish Socialist Workers’ Party (PSOE), founded in 1879, is Spain’s historic socialist party and a central actor from Restoration politics through the Second Republic, Francoist exile, and democratic transition. Headquartered on Madrid’s Calle de Ferraz, it rebuilt as a catch-all social-democratic party under Felipe González.

PSOE governments modernised Spain within the European Community, navigating regional autonomies, economic liberalisation, and later corruption and polarisation crises. Its rivalry with the People’s Party structured democratic Spain’s party system.

The PSOE exemplifies Southern European socialism’s path from Marxist origins to EU-era social democracy.
